phase: Phase 4 Module 1: Application Service Layer, Authorization Hardening & Admin Workflow Foundation

findings.title: Privileged RPC PostgREST Exposure Closure via Forward Migration
findings.evidence: PostgreSQL default grants allow EXECUTE on functions created in public schema to PUBLIC/authenticated unless explicitly revoked. In Supabase, this exposes administrative stored procedures to HTTP POST /rest/v1/rpc/*.
findings.exploitability_impact: High. Any authenticated student possessing a valid JWT could directly invoke fn_publish_exam_paper or fn_reevaluate_paper_attempts over HTTP PostgREST API.
findings.before_behavior: Privilege catalog allowed authenticated role to execute fn_publish_exam_paper and fn_reevaluate_paper_attempts, relying solely on internal SQL Gate 0 logic.
findings.after_behavior: Explicit forward-only migration REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION ... FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated; GRANT EXECUTE TO service_role, postgres; catalog verification guarantees 0 grants.
findings.remediation: Created migration 20261012140000_revoke_authenticated_privileged_rpc and added test DB-19 in tests/database.test.mjs.
test_references: tests/database.test.mjs: DB-19 (19.1 Catalog Verification, 19.2 Permission Denied for authenticated, 19.3 Re-evaluation Permission Denied, 19.4 Direct postgres Success)
findings.residual_risk: None in database kernel. Live Supabase project requires migration deployment in Phase 5 release gate.

findings.title: Server-Side Administrative Session Guard with Account Suspension Enforcement
findings.evidence: Application service layers must not rely on unverified client headers or JWT claims alone. Server-side operations required strict JWT signature verification via supabase.auth.getUser(), ban/suspension enforcement via user.banned_until, and authoritative public.users role checking.
findings.exploitability_impact: High. Banned, suspended, or demoted users could execute administrative functions if role caching or client claims were trusted.
findings.before_behavior: No centralized typed administrative session guard existed in application layer prior to Phase 4 Module 1.
findings.after_behavior: assertAdminSession() cryptographically verifies session, rejects anonymous sessions, enforces banned_until and deleted_at, queries public.users table, and strictly checks dbUser.role === Role.ADMIN, failing closed with typed UnauthorizedError (401) and ForbiddenError (403).
findings.remediation: Implemented assertAdminSession() in src/lib/auth/session.ts and verified across 7 discrete unit test scenarios.

findings.title: Strict Input Validation Boundary & RFC 4122 v4 UUID Validation
findings.evidence: Administrative Server Actions receiving client arguments could pass malformed strings or SQL injection probes to database drivers without schema validation.
findings.exploitability_impact: Medium. Unvalidated inputs could cause unhandled driver exceptions, logging pollution, or unexpected database state.
findings.before_behavior: No formal validation schemas for administrative actions existed.
findings.after_behavior: Zod schemas enforce trimmed RFC 4122 v4 UUID strings and minimum character length on adjudication reasons before database execution.
findings.remediation: Created src/lib/admin/schemas.ts and verified via unit tests.

findings.title: Administrative Application Service & Safe Domain Error Sanitization
findings.evidence: Direct database error messages from PostgreSQL can leak internal table names, constraint details, hostnames, or credentials to end users.
findings.exploitability_impact: Medium. Information disclosure of database internals or sensitive error messages.
findings.before_behavior: No centralized service or error sanitizer existed for exam paper administrative operations.
findings.after_behavior: publishExamPaper and reevaluatePaperAttempts invoke stored procedures via parameterized queries with explicit verified admin UUIDs; mapDatabaseDomainError parses MCQJ-ERR-* domain codes into client-safe messages while masking all internal SQL and credentials under 500 status.
findings.remediation: Implemented src/lib/admin/service.ts with AdminServiceError and mapDatabaseDomainError; tested against domain error codes and sensitive error masking.
test_references: tests/admin-service.test.mjs: mapDatabaseDomainError, publishExamPaper, and reevaluatePaperAttempts tests

findings.title: Administrative Server Actions with Structured Responses & Cache Invalidation
findings.evidence: Next.js App Router forms and admin management dashboards require safe Server Actions returning structured { success, data, error } responses and invalidating Next.js cache paths upon successful state mutations.
findings.exploitability_impact: Low / Informational. Architecture foundation for administrative UI.
findings.before_behavior: No server actions existed for administrative workflows.
findings.after_behavior: Created publishExamPaperAction and reevaluatePaperAttemptsAction with revalidatePath('/admin/papers') and typed error handling.
findings.remediation: Implemented src/app/admin/actions.ts and verified via next build and TypeScript typecheck.
test_references: next build compilation and static page generation
findings.residual_risk: None. Ready for Phase 4 Module 2 UI integration.
